title: 子 Agent 在哪里运行，结果怎样回来

request_order: parent acknowledges two background launches and waits
quick-start child receives Read result and finishes
catalog child receives Bash result and finishes first
parent receives first completion and waits
parent receives second completion and summarizes

audiences: 第一次接触 PMA、想知道子 Agent 是否只是一个黑盒名称的用户
想理解 Claude Code 父级、子分支和异步完成事件的 Harness 使用者
需要核对自研 Harness 分支归属、工具结果与父级回流的开发者
teaching_contract.question: 父 Agent 怎样启动两个子 Agent、每个分支做了什么、异步完成结果又怎样回到父对话？
teaching_contract.takeaway: 父模型返回两个 Agent tool_use；Claude Code 启动独立子分支；每个子分支仍有自己的模型请求和工具闭环；异步完成以 task-notification 进入父级后续请求，父 Agent 等齐结果再汇总。PMA 用 Turn、Request 和多 Agent 看板把这些证据连在一起。
explicit_limits: The user explicitly asks for two subagents, so this trace does not prove autonomous delegation.
The real trace shows asynchronous background launch and staggered completion, but it is not a benchmark of parallel speedup.
Ordinary Claude Code subagents must not be described as directly communicating Agent Team members.
The parent receives child task results; the trace does not claim that it receives every internal child message verbatim.
Deterministic fake-upstream responses demonstrate protocol shape and Viewer behavior, not remote model quality.
This chapter does not demonstrate nested subagents.

facts: Request 1 contains two Agent tool_use blocks for the quick-start and catalog Explore tasks.
The quick-start child branch contains Requests 2 and 5; Request 2 calls Read and Request 5 receives the matching result before returning its summary.
The catalog child branch contains Requests 3 and 6; Request 3 calls a read-only Bash find command and Request 6 receives docs/guide.md plus docs/viewer.md before returning its summary.
Parent Request 4 receives two asynchronous launch-confirmation tool_result blocks and explicitly waits without predicting results.
The catalog child completes first. Its task-notification triggers parent Request 7, which says one child has returned and waits for the other.
The quick-start child completes later. Its task-notification triggers parent Request 8 and the final three-point summary.
Current PMA groups the experiment as 3 Turns and 8 Requests while keeping both child branches inside the multi-agent board.
The native completion payload is a system-generated task-notification, not a new human message.
The files README.md, docs/guide.md, and docs/viewer.md retain their pre-run SHA-256 values.

product_feedback.finding: For this asynchronous Claude Code 2.1.220 trace, the Viewer labels the Agent launch-confirmation tool_result in Request 4 as parent result return, while actual child completion arrives later as task-notification events in Requests 7 and 8.
product_feedback.documentation_action: The chapter distinguishes launch confirmation from completion notification and uses the parent waiting/final responses plus a sanitized native event example. It does not present the current return badge as proof of task completion.

review_notes: The first expanded-board draft focused the wrong vertical region; it was rejected after the 1024 review and redrawn against the real multi-agent header and branch tabs.
The corrected expanded-board scene now uses a short click pulse on the native expand control, then branch badges 1 and 2 in narration order with one 0.6-second crossfade.
The asynchronous comparison scene intentionally retains badge 1 when badge 2 appears because Turn 2 and Turn 3 must be compared together; dim_ms makes the older Turn visibly secondary.
The first Turn 2 dim checkpoint landed after the subtitle had begun saying Turn 3; the timing was moved one second earlier and the affected frames were regenerated at both sizes.
The final Response scene uses a click pulse on the real detail button followed by one evidence badge, avoiding redundant action numbering.
All other source-to-detail changes use crossfade handoffs so the previous badge does not remain as visual noise.
No arrows are used in v0.3; nearby badges, focus boxes, and click pulses communicate the relationships without crossing readable content.
The 1920x1080 CSS viewport was rendered and inspected in the in-app Browser; repository review frames are normalized to 1920x1080, while the underlying Viewer source remains native 2048x1056.
Badge digits are geometrically centered at both review sizes, and subtitles remain in the bottom-center film safe area.
annotation_rules: Badges 1, 2, 3, and 4 appear in narration order, never all at scene entry.
When focus moves, the previous badge either fades out with a 0.4-0.7 second crossfade or remains only when comparison or causality requires it.
Each overlay draft records appearance order, retention choice, and fade-out timing.
Use short focus boxes and nearby badges before adding an arrow; this chapter should not need arrows.
Every progressive state must be reviewed at 1920x1080 and 1024x576, not only as a final fully annotated frame.
